name: The Afghan Whigs
label: Sub Pop
lede: Greg Dulli wanted a band that sounded like the Temptations, the Band and Neil Young at once. He got it in Cincinnati, took it to a Seattle grunge label, and he's still at it forty years later.

eras.title: The bassist with the beard
eras.text: Greg Dulli came home to Cincinnati from film school and a Tower Records job in Los Angeles and started the Black Republicans. A bassist showed up at the gigs, the band got a new name, and a Seattle label listened.

years.big: I'm better than your bass player.
years.src: Stereogum: We've Got A File On You · Wikipedia: Greg Dulli
years.h: John Curley turns up at Black Republicans gigs with a beard and an opinion
years.p: Said to [[Greg Dulli|0b17f0c3-9e37-4863-ab92-2c5be31e6e53]] after a show in Cincinnati, as Dulli tells it. Dulli's answer was fine; Curley played bass on the band's first four records.
years.xp:
The Black Republicans were Dulli's band before the Afghan Whigs. He described them to Stereogum as two guitars, a drum machine and a clarinet, "Echo & The Bunnymen with a clarinet, but punk-rock style."

Dulli had dropped out of film school at the University of Cincinnati, moved to Los Angeles, worked at Tower Records on Sunset and tried acting. Seeing [[The Dream Syndicate|8577c385-d06a-4a64-b4e7-6ebf25f2cb20]] sent him back to Ohio to start a band.

years.src: Stereogum: We've Got A File On You · Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Curley names the band, as a dig at the Black Republicans
years.p: [[Greg Dulli|0b17f0c3-9e37-4863-ab92-2c5be31e6e53]], [[John Curley|1d7ed8e7-199f-4774-b7a2-99a0feebf55a]], effects-pedal guitarist [[Rick McCollum|24875099-22a5-45aa-aae1-bf341ffd7e59]] and drummer [[Steve Earle|ceed50f1-a8d7-443e-8204-392dcab13970]] become the Afghan Whigs. Curley's name plays on Dulli's old band.
years.xp:
According to Dulli the first rehearsal as a four-piece was Halloween 1986, and the first song they worked up was the Temptations' Psychedelic Shack. His target was a cross between the Band, the Temptations, and Neil Young with Crazy Horse.

McCollum was already known around Cincinnati for what he could do with a floor full of pedals.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Big Top Halloween comes out in 1,000 copies, pressed by the band
years.p: Big Top Halloween is on Ultrasuede, their own label. Dulli wrote half of it in Arizona after the Black Republicans broke up, and one copy reached Sub Pop's Jonathan Poneman.

years.src: Stereogum: We've Got A File On You · Sub Pop: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Sub Pop signs a second band from outside the Northwest
years.p: Only Denver's The Fluid got there first.
years.xp: Dulli has never been shy about the debt. "We don't get signed without them," he told Stereogum of the Fluid, and put it more plainly still: "The Fluid unleashed the Afghan Whigs."

eras.title: Soul, through a fuzz box
eras.text: On Sub Pop the Afghan Whigs sat next to Mudhoney and Nirvana and sounded like a Motown record played through a fuzz pedal. Congregation found the voice, MTV found the videos, and Elektra found the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Up in It · Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Sub Pop puts out Up in It, with Nirvana's producer at the desk
years.p: The band's second album and first for Sub Pop, largely produced by [[Jack Endino|d06cca33-9167-4049-b5ce-6a6aeff60a8d]]. Retarded becomes a college-radio hit.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: A Sub Pop package tour sends Cincinnati out with Seattle and Boston
years.p: To support Up in It, the Afghan Whigs go out on a bill with [[Mudhoney|e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc]] and Boston's Bullet LaVolta.

years.src: Wikipedia: Congregation
years.h: Dulli records "Miles Iz Ded" on the day Miles Davis dies
years.p: At Ultrasuede in Cincinnati he cuts a hidden track for Congregation, built around a message from label man David Katznelson.

years.src: Wikipedia: Congregation
years.h: A $15,000 Sub Pop advance buys Congregation in three cities
years.p: Made July to September 1991 at Bear Creek near Seattle, in Los Angeles and in Cincinnati. Soul, psychedelic sprawl and punk in one band, with Dulli co-producing.
years.xp:
The cover photo shows a nude Black woman on a blanket holding a white baby, read by many as a comment on the band's debt to Black music. Dulli co-produced with Ross Ian Stein.

It didn't chart, but the videos for Turn On the Water and Conjure Me got onto MTV, and the band toured North America and Europe, including dates with [[Teenage Fanclub|e6f8912b-7df9-4aae-b551-2cd03dc29588]].

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Uptown Avondale is an EP of Supremes covers
years.p: Named for a Cincinnati neighborhood, with the Supremes songs done the Afghan Whigs way. The Conjure Me single carries a Supremes cover too.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Elektra signs the Afghan Whigs
years.p: Congregation has MTV play and a cult following; that's enough for a major label.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes a bidding war, with the deal including a clause to fund a feature film Dulli had scripted. The film was never made.

eras.title: Gentlemen, and the dark after it
eras.text: On a major label Dulli made a breakup record where the narrator is the one doing the damage. Gentlemen is the one people press on their friends; Black Love went further in, into noir and crime scenes.

years.cap: Greg Dulli, John Curley, Rick McCollum and Steve Earle
years.src: Wikipedia: Gentlemen · Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Gentlemen, cut at Ardent, Big Star's studio in Memphis
years.p: Dulli produced it himself at Ardent Studios and Ultrasuede. A song cycle about a relationship going bad, under an ironic title.
years.xp:
The cover is modeled on Nan Goldin's 1983 photo Nan and Brian in Bed. Wikipedia says Linda Ronstadt, also on Elektra, objected to it as close to pornographic.

Debonair went Top 20 on the Modern Rock chart. The album placed No. 17 in the Village Voice Pazz & Jop poll, drew good notices from Rolling Stone, and by 1996 had sold 130,000 US copies.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gentlemen · Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Dulli hands "My Curse" to Marcy Mays
years.p: The lyrics, about the violent end of a relationship, were so personal Dulli couldn't sing them. [[Scrawl|c5e3744d-b321-4cc9-976a-4d4d9d0ee73a]]'s [[Marcy Mays|5aac1027-892f-4d12-8dc3-ebb54de02a3c]] takes the lead on Gentlemen.
years.xp: Mays had already sung on the Afghan Whigs' Ornament single. On My Curse a woman voices the man's side of the story, which suits an album whose narrator is the problem.

years.src: Stereogum: We've Got A File On You · Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Dulli hangs up on Don Was, then ends up singing Lennon
years.p: Hungover in a hotel room, he took the call for a prank. He went on to sing most leads on the Backbeat soundtrack with [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]], [[Thurston Moore|8ba48525-d922-42ee-9775-97b7b8f9712e]], [[Mike Mills|525d2a4a-3d81-4d96-9581-3442feed3d2e]] and Don Fleming.
years.xp:
Dulli told Stereogum what he said to Was: "I'm pretty sure I literally said, 'Fuck off!' and hung up. I thought somebody was pranking me."

The band cut the whole Beatles-in-Hamburg soundtrack live in two days.

years.src: Stereogum: We've Got A File On You · Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Foo Fighters' debut has exactly one guest, and it's Dulli
years.p: Dave Grohl asked him to play guitar in an afternoon session. Besides Grohl, Dulli is the only credited musician on Foo Fighters, and he says he barely remembers it.
years.xp: The session was at Bob Lang's studio outside Seattle. Dulli told Stereogum that Grohl played him some of the songs and he went to see him at his house, but the day itself is a blur.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Steve Earle is out after Gentlemen
years.p: Paul Buchignani takes over the drums as the Afghan Whigs start Black Love in Seattle and Memphis.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Black Love goes to the crime scene
years.p: Dulli's noir record peaks at No. 79 on the Billboard 200. Blame, Etc. draws on the life of Temptations singer David Ruffin.
years.xp:
Dulli pulled from James Ellroy's crime novels, the Coen brothers' Blood Simple, Kenneth Anger's Hollywood Babylon and Weegee's crime-scene photos. Crime Scene Part One was reportedly influenced by an unmade script for The Million Dollar Hotel.

Wikipedia says critics praised the record for catching the band's live power, and that its commercial disappointment and reported neglect from Elektra ended the relationship.

years.src: Stereogum: We've Got A File On You · Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: The Afghan Whigs play the bar band in Beautiful Girls
years.p: Dulli's best friend Ted Demme directed the film and Dulli executive-produced the soundtrack. The band plays Barry White's Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe in a minor key.
years.xp: Demme asked for the Afghan Whigs as the bar band, and Dulli rearranged the Barry White song in a minor key. They also cover Frederick Knight's Be For Real on the soundtrack.

eras.title: A fractured skull and a press release
eras.text: Dulli moved to New Orleans, started the Twilight Singers and made 1965, the band's loosest, sexiest record. Then a fight outside an Austin club put him in the hospital, and two years later the band ended by press release.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Dulli moves into Peter Buck's house in New Orleans
years.p: He rents the [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] guitarist's place and starts [[The Twilight Singers|53a4de34-35ca-4ad0-aa4b-67382435ed69]] with local players. Michael Horrigan takes the Afghan Whigs' drum stool.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: 1965 is named for the year Dulli and Curley were born
years.p: Recorded at Daniel Lanois' New Orleans studio for Columbia, with film noir and Nas in the mix. The band tours it as Aerosmith's opener.

years.src: Austin Chronicle · MTV News · Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Dulli's skull is fractured outside Liberty Lunch in Austin
years.p: After an Afghan Whigs show he fought a stagehand and hit his head on the pavement. The club blamed Dulli; the band disputed it and sued.
years.xp:
The Austin Chronicle ran the club's version. Co-manager Mileah Jordan said "Dulli was the aggressor, first threatening and then attacking a stagehand." The paper reported that he stayed after closing and went at the stagehand with a two-by-four before the worker hit him once. Police corroborated the stagehand's account, and no charges were filed.

Dulli was treated at Brackenridge Hospital; Wikipedia says he was left in a coma. MTV News later reported the band suing the club. He was back on tour within two months.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: A press release ends the Afghan Whigs
years.p: The band hadn't played since September 1999. The statement blames distance and family obligations; Dulli calls it amicable, and soon co-buys the Short Stop bar in Los Angeles.
years.xp: Dulli later said it wasn't necessarily an "official breakup," which is how the 2006 session and the 2011 reunion read in hindsight.

eras.title: See it now, or never
eras.text: Two new songs for a best-of, five years of silence, then a festival promoter made the call. The reunion was billed as one time only and turned into a second career.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Four of them get back in a room for two new songs
years.p: I'm a Soldier and Magazine are cut for Unbreakable: A Retrospective 1990–2006, out on Rhino on June 5, 2007.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: A festival press release brings the Afghan Whigs back
years.p: All Tomorrow's Parties announces the band for its events: the first time they've worked together since 2006.

years.cap: Greg Dulli, John Curley and Rick McCollum on the reunion tour, Tel Aviv, June 2012
q: We're doing this one time: See it now, or never see it again.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs · Cincinnati Magazine: The Afghan Whigs Celebrate 40 Years
years.h: The reunion tour starts at the Bowery Ballroom
years.p: A day after Jimmy Fallon, the Afghan Whigs play Manhattan. Newsday called it possibly the band's greatest concert ever; the tour reaches sixteen countries.
years.xp:
On Fallon, May 22, they played See and Don't See, a 1970 soul song by Marie "Queenie" Lyons, and I'm Her Slave. Guitarist [[Dave Rosser|fd7c487f-f0fb-4fd1-b639-b5f3dcfa7742]] and multi-instrumentalist Rick Nelson came in for the reunion.

SPIN's Steve Kandell wrote that Dulli, at 47, was leaner, fitter and in better voice than in the band's heyday.

years.cap: Greg Dulli at Primavera Sound, Barcelona, May 2012
years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: The Afghan Whigs give away their Frank Ocean cover
years.p: A free download of [[Frank Ocean|e520459c-dff4-491d-a6e4-c97be35e0044]]'s Lovecrimes, already a staple of the reunion shows.

years.cap: The Afghan Whigs on stage, March 2013
years.src: Stereogum: We've Got A File On You · Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Usher sings with the Afghan Whigs at SXSW
years.p: He heard the Frank Ocean cover and asked them to back him at the Fader Fort. Dulli says he had to fix Usher's words in rehearsal.
years.xp: Curley said that set made it likely the band would record again.

eras.title: Back on Sub Pop, minus old friends
eras.text: The second act now runs as long as the first. It brought three albums, a return to the label that signed them, and the loss of Rick McCollum from the band and Dave Rosser from the world.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs · NPR First Listen
years.h: The Afghan Whigs announce Rick McCollum is out
years.p: It comes ahead of the band's first album in 16 years. His pedal-soaked guitar had defined the sound.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs · NPR First Listen · Sub Pop: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Back on Sub Pop, Do to the Beast debuts at No. 32
years.p: The band's first Top 40 album. Guests include Usher's musical director Johnny Najera, Mark McGuire of Emeralds and Queens of the Stone Age's Alain Johannes.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Twenty-one years on, Gentlemen scores 95 on Metacritic
years.p: The deluxe reissue Gentlemen at 21 gets the best reviews of the band's career. [[Patrick Keeler|0cb67e93-6b5f-4433-971c-6d4adb60d3d8]] of [[The Raconteurs|be407b02-f3e6-4ed5-9489-f8e5f0ab36dc]] is now on drums.

years.src: Sub Pop: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: A week at Rick Nelson's studio gets In Spades half done
years.p: The studio is Marigny Sound in New Orleans. Dulli calls Prince, who died the year before, his North Star.

years.cap: The Afghan Whigs at Haldern Pop Festival, Germany, August 2017
years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs · Cincinnati Magazine: The Afghan Whigs Celebrate 40 Years
years.h: Dave Rosser dies of colon cancer at 50
years.p: He had played with the band since the 2011 reunion and on both new albums, and died weeks after In Spades came out.
years.xp: Rosser was also a member of the Twilight Singers lineup. Wikipedia gives his death as June 28, 2017, after a long illness.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs · Cincinnati Magazine: The Afghan Whigs Celebrate 40 Years
years.h: How Do You Burn? arrives with a song in Gran Turismo 7
years.p: The first Afghan Whigs album in five years, on BMG. Blind Melon's Christopher Thorn joins on guitar.
years.xp: The lead single, I'll Make You See God, came out in February 2022 and lands on the Gran Turismo 7 soundtrack.

years.src: Cincinnati Magazine: The Afghan Whigs Celebrate 40 Years
years.h: Forty years in, the Afghan Whigs go home to Bogart's
years.p: The 40th-anniversary show in Cincinnati has drummer Bryan Lee Brown in for Keeler.
years.xp: Cincinnati Magazine reported that Keeler became unavailable because of his work with Jack White's band. Brown is a film composer and friend of Dulli's who contributed to the new record, and a teaser track, House of I, was already streaming.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Afghan Whigs
years.h: Soft Control becomes the fourth album since the reunion
years.p: The lead single, Jungle Roux, came out in June.
